perspective:
Christian Mensah’s available information:

- He knows Jonathan Balogun is his childhood best friend. They are close, and Christian often seeks Jonathan’s advice and values his perspective.
- Christian has recently perceived Jonathan acting differently and felt anxious and suspicious that Jonathan was hiding something important. He arranged a meeting at their favorite coffee shop to confront him.
- At the meeting, Christian told Jonathan he felt something serious was being hidden. He heard Jonathan say he could trust him, then Jonathan admitted he had been keeping something back: he is in some trouble and did not know how to tell Christian.
- Christian felt worried and empathetic. He offered help, said they could face it together, and asked what Jonathan needed. He heard Jonathan say the situation is complicated, that he did not want to drag Christian into it, but that he could use support and resources to get out of the mess.
- Christian began to believe the trouble might involve criminal activity. He asked Jonathan directly whether it was illegal. He heard Jonathan say he could not say for sure, that he might have gotten involved with the wrong people, but that he did not do anything illegal himself.
- Christian decided to investigate discreetly. Jonathan thanked him and said he trusted Christian to handle it carefully.
- Through his own investigation, Christian came to believe/found that Jonathan was being framed. He told Jonathan he had leads but did not yet know who was responsible, and he planned to gather more evidence to prove Jonathan’s innocence.
- Later, Christian found out/determined that the person behind it is someone both he and Jonathan know and trust. He felt betrayed and resolute. He told Jonathan he would confront this person and seek justice. Jonathan warned him the person is dangerous but said he trusted Christian to do what is right.
- Christian has access to his own feelings, statements, decisions, investigative findings, and interactions listed above. He does not have access to other characters’ private thoughts, hidden events, or facts he did not observe, hear, or learn through his own investigation.
